text: Refactoring is the process of improving code structure without changing its external behavior. The goal is not to add new features but to make the existing code easier to read, understand, and maintain. By breaking down long functions, renaming unclear variables, or removing duplicated logic, developers reduce technical debt—the hidden cost of messy code. This careful cleanup makes future changes faster and safer, as a clean structure helps you spot bugs more easily. Think of it as tidying a toolbox: you don’t buy new tools, but you arrange them so that the right one is always in reach. Good refactoring keeps a project healthy for the long run.
